frozenTask.learnerTask: Compare held ends with resected ends aligned at short matching sequence, without equating a junction pattern with enzyme dependence.
frozenTask.gap: The existing branched Mermaid captures end-handling alternatives, but it cannot show the DNA sequence removed between short matches or a compatible direct join. Two DNA-end strips would teach the central structural contrast and can reuse the repair-overview style.

sequenceTeaching.origin: Invented author toy; not a paper construct, tumor sequence or measured outcome
sequenceTeaching.indexing: Positions 1–14 in top strand read left-to-right 5′→3′; bottom same spatial orientation 3′→5′

before.break: Both strands broken between positions 7 and 8; undamaged ligatable blunt ends with appropriate 3′OH/5′phosphate chemistry assumed

repeats.alignedComplement: CTG, read left-to-right 3′→5′ on the other end; not GAC paired with GAC

selectedResection.left: Remove bottom 5′-ending strand positions 3–7; left top positions 3–7 remain as 3′ tail GACTT. Left duplex stub positions 1–2 remains CA/GT.
selectedResection.right: Remove top 5′-starting strand positions 8–12; right bottom positions 8–12 remain as 3′ tail TTCTG when displayed left-to-right 3′→5′. Right duplex stub positions 13–14 remains GT/CA.
selectedResection.limits: Exact five-base trimming on each end is an author toy schematic, not a measured or universally required resection length.

alignment.left3primeUnpairedTail: TT, top positions 6–7, curls away on upper right
alignment.right3primeUnpairedTail: TT, bottom positions 8–9, curls away on lower left
alignment.rule: Pair A:T and G:C with opposing strand polarities; curve both unmatched 3′ flaps away rather than drawing them paired. No ligase connects unmatched flaps in this intermediate.

shortMatchJoin.deletionLogicalRepresentation: Positions 6–12: TTAAGAC; loss of TTAA interval plus one GAC repeat. Repeat provenance is ambiguous after annealing; chosen bookkeeping representation does not identify which physical repeat molecule survived.
shortMatchJoin.synthesis: No gap-filling synthesis is required for this exact toy. After removal of both unmatched TT flaps, the surviving top supplies CA+GAC and GT, and the surviving bottom supplies GT and CTG+CA; every one of the seven final spatial slots is paired. Two backbone nicks remain: top between final positions 5/6 and bottom between final positions 2/3. Seal these nicks. Other end structures can leave single-stranded gaps that require synthesis; no new-synthesis color or region belongs in this toy.

teachingCopy.alt: Four stacked scenes show a fourteen-base-pair blunt break and unchanged direct join, one connected GAC/CTG alignment with two unpaired TT flaps, and a seven-base-pair short-match product. A small transition symbol shows two backbone nicks after trimming, with all seven positions paired. A bracket counts TTAA plus one GAC as seven base pairs lost.
teachingCopy.caption: For these selected toy ends, direct joining retains all 14 base pairs; short-match joining retains 7. Removing the two unmatched TT flaps leaves two nicks to seal, with no gap filling needed for this toy. Other end structures can require synthesis. Colors and protein shapes are teaching conventions. A short match or deletion does not establish Polθ dependence; these examples are not a universal menu of repair routes.
teachingCopy.workedExercise: Look at the toy sequence: `CA–GAC–TT|AA–GAC–GT` before joining and `CA–GAC–GT` after the short-match example. The vertical bar marks the break; all letters are read along the top strand from 5′ to 3′. How many base pairs were lost, and does the remaining GAC identify Polθ?
teachingCopy.workedAnswer: **Worked answer:** seven base pairs are lost: the four-base `TTAA` interval plus one three-base `GAC` repeat. The repaired duplex contains one GAC match, rather than two copies stacked on top of each other. This count describes a selected fictional product. After the two unmatched TT tails are removed, all seven base pairs are present; two backbone nicks remain to seal. It does not establish Polθ dependence; factor-specific perturbations, repair measurements, controls and, where feasible, rescue are needed.

sources.label: Bennardo et al. 2008
sources.accessMethod: Actual HTTP 200 NLM primary article BioC XML; rendered web discovery attempts qualified separately
sources.depth: Publisher HTML abstract, introduction, selected EJ5/EJ2 results, figure captions and discussion personally read. Private BioC copy retained; no source figure pixels or supplementary junction tables inspected.
sources.paraphrasedSupport: Engineered mammalian reporters relate short repeats and deletion products to tested factor requirements. Broader alternative-joining names describe overlapping sets of events; a junction alone does not establish a unique enzyme.

sources.label: Kent et al. 2015
sources.accessMethod: Actual HTTP 200 NLM primary article BioC XML; rendered web discovery attempts qualified separately
sources.depth: Selected introduction, biochemical substrate/results and discussion read through actual NLM BioC XML; not complete supplemental constructs or rescue evidence. U2OS is interpreted from paper model, not generalized to patients.
sources.paraphrasedSupport: Purified human Polθ polymerase-domain substrates and a human U2OS reporter with POLQ knockdown support microhomology annealing/extension in those systems. Short matches can be terminal or internal. Factor-specific results are stronger than visual junction similarity.

sources.label: Wyatt et al. 2016
sources.accessMethod: Actual HTTP 200 NLM primary article BioC XML; rendered web discovery attempts qualified separately
sources.depth: Selected abstract, pre-resected-substrate results and discussion read from NLM BioC XML. Suggested nuclease identities are not proven in this source and will not be labeled in the art; model thresholds will not be taught as universal.
sources.paraphrasedSupport: Mouse cell/substrate perturbation work supports 3′ overhang joining with microhomology search, nonhomologous-tail removal and synthesis. Polθ itself has no intrinsic nuclease activity. Residual alternative joining remains in double-deficient cells.

sources.label: Stinson et al. 2024
sources.accessMethod: Actual HTTP 200 NLM primary article BioC XML; rendered web discovery attempts qualified separately
sources.depth: Selected abstract, blunt-substrate results and preparation methods read from NLM BioC XML; not all figures/data or human patient material. Depicted proteins are simplified role symbols, not measured molecular stoichiometry.
sources.paraphrasedSupport: Xenopus egg extract, factor depletion/reconstitution and blunt-end single-molecule work support a ligation-ready NHEJ complex and compatible blunt-end repair. This supplies direct construct support for the selected blunt toy ends.
